title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: Bangladesh is navigating post-pandemic recovery, climate challenges, and technological shifts while preparing for LDC graduation by 2026. Despite steady growth and private investment, major challenges persist, job creation is lagging economic expansion, informal employment dominates, women and marginalized groups remain underrepresented in quality jobs, and private sector capacity for responsible, inclusive, and green business practices are limited. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) struggle with productivity, regulatory compliance, and formalization, limiting their potential for growth and decent work. Bangladesh Employers’ Federation (BEF) is exploring opportunities to facilitate partnerships with like-minded business chambers to be engaged in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) process. This resulted in the setting up of the Bangladesh Private Sector Working Committee (BPSWC) consisting of BEF, and Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of commerce (FBCCI) to work with the UN, government and other stakeholders for the promotion of SDGs. The Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for BPSWC was signed on May 2023, signifying strategic alliances and unified representation of the private sector to promote SDGs. ILO helped BEF to conduct a study on the private sector contribution to SDGs, and in the formulation of an advocacy strategy through focussed group discussions and consultations with members of the BPSWC. ILO’s strategy also focuses on advancing labour reforms, supporting decent work, promoting gender-responsive enterprise development, and fostering social protection systems, implemented in partnership with ministries including Labour and Employment, Industry, and Youth & Sports, as well as employers’ organizations, chamber of commerce, industry associations, development partners and UN agencies.
